title: A reader holding the runtime store for over five seconds fails the running step
description: The flywheel's runtime store (flywheel.py, sqlite3.connect(path)) uses SQLite's default rollback journal and Python's default 5-second busy timeout. Any other process reading runtime.sqlite3 with a query that scans for more than five seconds holds a shared lock long enough that the writer's commit raises sqlite3.OperationalError, which fails the step and stops a replay. Seen in the 1,200-cycle editorial study (attempt 4, decision-flywheel-8f3a052a): at cycle 1125 a rubric step failed with OperationalError a few seconds after a read-only progress query (7 s full-table json_extract scan of the 1.3 GB log) ran against the same file; disk was not full at the time (3 to 7 GB free), so the lock is the likely cause. Fix: open the runtime store in WAL mode (as web_store.py already does) so readers never block the writer, and set a longer busy timeout. Acceptance: a spec holds a read transaction open on the store for longer than the busy timeout while a step commits, and the step succeeds.
